newsitem.title: USA: Consumer protections in US Treasury bank proposal.
newsitem.headline: Consumer protections in US Treasury bank proposal.

text.p: The following consumer protection steps were part of the U.S. Treasury Department's proposal on banking modernization that was released Wednesday:

-- Banking agencies, in consultation with the Securities and Exchange Commission, would be required to prescribe rules regarding banks' retail sales of nondeposit investment products, in order to avoid customer confusion about the nature and applicability of Federal Deposit Insurance Corp and Securities Investor Protection Corp insurance, and to protect against conflicts of interest and other abuses.
-- Such rules would address matters such as sales practices, qualifications of sales personnel, incentive compensation, and referrals.
-- The rules would require simple, direct and understandable disclosures, such as the following:
-- Customers could prevent sharing of confidential customer information between banks and their nonbank affiliates.
-- The proposed National Council on Financial services would periodically assess the effectiveness of such regulations, and could adopt regulations more stringent than those of the agencies.
